messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Prefill GPU OOM spike detected in cluster-gpu-us-west-2 — multiple container restarts. Paging oncall. <http://incident.link/6187654321|Incident 6187654321> :rotating_light:

mike (oncall): onit, seeing alerts. pulling logs now

olga (sre): same, CPU+GPU node group showing restarts on node-17 and node-19. probable prefill OOM from long-context requests

jin (ml-runtime): i can confirm logs show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` during prefill phase. one container got Exit 137 then restarted. snippet: ```2026-03-18T04:12:10Z model-runtime ERROR CUDA out of memory when allocating 2.3G for KV cache. Backtrace... Container killed (OOM)```

mike (oncall): customers: some high-qPS tenants reported 500s and truncated responses. luis can you start a customer impact check?

luis (cust-ops): pinged 3 affected accounts (enterprise, ecommerce) — they see failures for large doc uploads / long prompts. told them we're investigating and will provide ETA.

sara (eng-infra): quick triage: node kernel logs show OOM killer targeting process `model-server` then kubelet restarting pod. disk and network look healthy.

jin (ml-runtime): mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily route long-window requests to cold-model variant (lower KV prefetch), 2) push runtime flag to reduce max_prefetch_kv from 8 -> 2, 3) enable aggressive KV eviction for affected pools

olga (sre): agree. doing (2) now via k8s rollout patch to configmap `runtime-prefetch` -> `{max_prefetch_kv: 2}`. will monitor mem usage.

mike (oncall): while that rolls, enable route fallback for customer tiers to `model-small` for requests > 32k tokens. jin, can you flip the routing flag?

jin (ml-runtime): flipping feature-flag `route-large-to-cold` -> `true`. applying policy to clusters us-west-2, us-west-1. patch done.

sara (eng-infra): scaling note: autoscaler currently set to 0.5 scale-per-minute to avoid noisy neighbor. temporarily bumping to 1.5 to absorb remaining steady load

olga (sre): memory graphs show immediate drop in KV allocations after max_prefetch change. pod restarts stopped within 4 minutes of the patch.

luis (cust-ops): update to customers: sent note — intermittent failures reduced, fallback to smaller model applied, follow-up summary to come. they appreciate the quick workaround.

mike (oncall): next steps: 1) leave `max_prefetch_kv=2` until we validate model patch with quantized KV, 2) add a short-term circuit-breaker to reject >64k token prefill, 3) run backfill to rehydrate caches slowly

jin (ml-runtime): opened PR for quantized-KV hotfix and ticket to add per-tenant prefetch budgeting. link: http://git/repo/PR-4321

sara (eng-infra): recording incident note. node-17 was cordoned and pods drained, will reintroduce after soak.

olga (sre): handing to next oncall (tomorrow) — @mike please add runbook checklist: what we patched, patch IDs, customer list, rollback steps.

mike (oncall): adding checklist now in postmortem doc. summary: prefills from vlong-context jobs caused KV blowout; mitigated with prefetch cap + routing fallback + autoscaler bump. total customer-facing time ~12m. handing off to olga for post-incident followthrough.

olga (sre): ack. I'll run the postmortem and coordinate cust follow-ups. closing the active pager. :white_check_mark:
